summary: The paper introduces Neighbor Distance Minimization (NDM), an unsupervised method that learns an orthogonal rotation of a model's representation space so that neighbor distances within resulting subspaces are minimized, yielding a non-basis-aligned decomposition. The authors motivate the objective through a feature-group/mutual-exclusiveness view (with a total-correlation interpretation), validate on a toy superposition model, quantitatively evaluate against known GPT-2 Small circuits (IOI, Greater-than) using subspace patching and Gini-coefficient concentration metrics against five unsupervised baselines, and provide qualitative preimage analyses plus a 2B-scale demonstration on Qwen2.5-1.5B and Gemma-2-2B for context vs. parametric knowledge routing. The direction is timely and the results are meaningful evidence that unsupervised decompositions can recover circuit-relevant variables, though the evaluation is narrow (one small model for the quantitative suite, five hand-picked tests), the dimension-selection procedure and hyperparameter sensitivity are only partially characterized, and statistical treatment (seeds, error bars) is largely absent.
strengths: Genuinely novel unsupervised objective for finding non-basis-aligned subspaces; contrasts cleanly with supervised DAS and with SAE-style sparse-feature decompositions, and the total-correlation/MI reinterpretation is a satisfying theoretical framing.

Quantitative evaluation is grounded in known circuits (IOI, Greater-than) with a principled use of subspace interchange interventions and a clearly justified Gini-coefficient metric (with a calibration threshold argued in App. D.4); NDM beats PCA, random, identity, and an SAE-feature-clustering baseline on average.

Nice qualitative story: preimage analysis shows distinct subspaces at the same layer encoding current token, prior token, position, and topic, with consistency across inputs — plausibly the kind of 'variables' the paper claims.

Scaling demonstration on 2B-parameter models with a well-designed double counterfactual (Param Corrupt vs. Context Corrupt) provides convincing dissociation evidence that individual subspaces mediate distinct knowledge-routing mechanisms.
The paper is honest about several limitations (dimension granularity, reliance on Linear Representation Hypothesis, unclear interpretation of small subspaces).

key_concerns.issue: Statistical treatment is thin: Table 1 reports point estimates with no seeds, error bars, or significance tests; the ablation is deferred to appendix and the sensitivity of NDM's outputs to the merging threshold, subspace-init dimension, and random init of R is not quantified in the main text. Given that some NDM entries are close to baselines on individual tests, it is hard to know how robust the 0.71 average advantage is.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over multiple seeds for NDM and all baselines on each test, and add a paired test or bootstrap CI on the average. Move a compact version of the hyperparameter sensitivity into the main body.

key_concerns.issue: The quantitative circuit evaluation rests entirely on GPT-2 Small and only 5 tests drawn from two circuits (IOI, Greater-than). The paper's claim that NDM finds 'variable-like' subspaces would be much stronger with at least one additional model family or one additional circuit (e.g., indirect object identification variants, docstring, arithmetic-carry) evaluated in the same framework.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one more model (e.g., Pythia-160M/410M) or circuit to the quantitative suite; alternatively, run the same subspace-patching protocol against ground-truth interventions on the 2B models to make the scaling claim quantitative rather than qualitative.

key_concerns.issue: The dimension-configuration procedure (start-small-then-merge with an MI threshold via KSG) is presented as central to the method but its impact is under-analyzed. Different thresholds could produce very different partitions and interpretations; App. G.4 alternatives are alluded to but the main text does not show how much downstream Gini scores or qualitative interpretations depend on this choice.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Include a main-text figure showing test-suite performance as a function of the MI threshold and initial subspace size, and a comparison against the App. G.4 alternatives.

key_concerns.issue: The 2B-scale results (Fig. 5) are presented as dissociation evidence, but there is no baseline table analogous to Table 1 in the main text — App. figures are referenced but not summarized. The reader cannot easily judge whether PCA/random/feature-clustering baselines also find dissociating subspaces at 2B.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a compact quantitative summary in the main text (e.g., a small table of clean-vs-Param-Corrupt-vs-Context-Corrupt patching effects for the top-k subspaces of NDM and each baseline), not just a pointer to appendix figures.

key_concerns.issue: The 'feature group / mutual exclusiveness' motivation is presented as an ideal-case justification, but the argument that neighbor distance minimization recovers such a partition is intuitive rather than proved. A more formal statement (even a proposition under stated assumptions on the toy model) would strengthen the theoretical framing.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a short proposition in App. B making explicit the conditions under which the NDM objective's minimum coincides with the correct group-aligned rotation, or clearly state it as a conjecture with empirical support.

key_concerns.issue: The preimage-based qualitative interpretation is bounded by a 4000-sequence corpus and a fixed cosine-similarity threshold (0.85). This may cherry-pick coherent-looking preimages; the paper does not report how often subspaces resist any human interpretation.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report the fraction of subspaces (per layer) whose top-K preimages admit a consistent human label, ideally with a small inter-rater exercise; discuss the sensitivity of qualitative results to the similarity threshold.

key_concerns.issue: Related work is reasonable but does not sharply differentiate NDM from concurrent unsupervised subspace-finding techniques (e.g., ICA-style methods on activations, non-negative matrix factorization on residual streams, or SAE feature-cluster subspaces beyond the one adapted from Engels et al. 2024).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph explicitly contrasting NDM with ICA and NMF applied to activations, and discuss why the neighbor-distance objective is expected to differ from these on non-Gaussian, structured feature distributions.

key_concerns.issue: Clarity: Eq. (2)-(4) are typeset poorly (partition rendered as a stack, minR1N appears to be a rendering artifact), and Table 1 is essentially unreadable in the plain-text extraction (numbers run together without column separators). Some readers may struggle to follow the exact objective from the main text alone.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Rewrite the optimization block with cleaner notation and reformat Table 1 for clear column alignment (or split into per-metric subtables).

questions_for_authors: How stable is the learned partition (both R and the dimension configuration c) across random seeds of R initialization? Do you get essentially the same subspaces, or is there mode collapse / degeneracy?
How sensitive is the Table 1 average Gini to the MI merging threshold? Is there a value at which NDM's advantage over baselines disappears?

The Feature (SAE-cluster) baseline is the closest competitor on average (0.56 vs 0.71). Can you characterize where NDM specifically wins over it — is it primarily on the small subspaces where SAE clustering has fewer features per cluster?

For the 2B-model results: what happens if you apply the same protocol to PCA-based partitions with matched dimension configurations? Do baselines also show dissociation, and how much less clean is it than NDM?

Do you see evidence that NDM's found subspaces at one layer relate cleanly to subspaces at adjacent layers (i.e., can you already begin to trace a 'subspace circuit'), or is the partition largely independent across layers?
How does the choice of Euclidean vs cosine distance in Eq. (3) actually affect real-model results — you mention cosine underperforms in the toy setting, but is that also true for GPT-2?
What is the runtime scaling of NDM as a function of d (residual dimension) and N (activation count)? App. H is referenced but a main-text one-liner would help judge scalability claims.
calibration_check: Claims are mostly appropriately scoped — the authors repeatedly caveat the 2B-scale results and acknowledge granularity/interpretation limits — though 'strong connection between subspaces and circuit variables' is somewhat strong given only 5 tests on one small model.

significance.justification: An unsupervised route to non-basis-aligned, causally meaningful subspaces is a real contribution to mech-interp; if the method holds up, it enables input-independent subspace circuits, which is a direction the community is actively pursuing.

novelty.justification: The neighbor-distance-minimization objective for learning orthogonal partitions of representation space is genuinely new relative to DAS (supervised), SAEs (sparse feature basis), and PCA/ICA; the total-correlation reframing is a nice theoretical bridge.

rigor.justification: Toy validation is clean, causal-intervention protocol is appropriate, and baselines are reasonable, but the argument that NDM converges to feature-group-aligned subspaces is heuristic rather than proved, and the merging procedure introduces additional degrees of freedom that are under-controlled in the main text.

statistical_soundness.justification: Table 1 and Fig. 5 report point estimates with no seed averaging, error bars, or significance tests, which is below the ICLR bar for a method paper whose central claim rests on a ~0.15 Gini gap over baselines.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations (dimension granularity, LRH reliance, uninterpretable small subspaces, uncertainty at 2B) are stated openly; the abstract's claim of 'strong connection' is defensible given the Gini > 0.6 threshold argument, though slightly optimistic.

clarity.justification: Intuition and motivation are conveyed well, but the formal objective is typeset awkwardly, and Table 1 is hard to parse; several algorithmic details are deferred to the appendix in ways that hurt the main-text argument.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure with Motivation, Method, Toy Experiments, LM Experiments (quantitative + qualitative + scaling), Discussion, Conclusion; length appears appropriate.

reproducibility.justification: The core algorithm, KSG-based merging, distance choice, activation sources, patching protocol, and hyperparameters (thresholds, MiniPile counts, layer/position choices) are described in a way that a competent group could reasonably reimplement, though many key details live in appendices and multiple sensitivity choices would need to be re-derived.

related_work.justification: Coverage of components, SAEs, and prior subspace work is broad and current, but the delineation from ICA/NMF-style unsupervised decompositions and from concurrent SAE-cluster subspace methods is underdeveloped.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative and claim-supporting displays (RW before/after in the toy, preimages illustrating distinct semantic roles per subspace, Fig. 5 showing dissociation on 2B models); the ensemble supports rather than decorates the argument, though Table 1's readability is a concern.

breadth_generality.justification: Quantitative circuit evaluation is limited to GPT-2 Small and 5 tests from 2 circuits; the 2B extension is a single mechanism (context vs parametric routing) shown mainly qualitatively. Generality claims outrun the evidence somewhat.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a fresh, well-motivated method with genuine causal evidence and a scaling demonstration, held back by weak statistical treatment and narrow quantitative breadth. Fits the profile of a paper that could clear the bar with modest revision.
